title: Python
description: Can write idiomatic Python that handles invalid input and ships with tests — and can package a project so a clean checkout installs and runs from the README.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can write small CLI programs with functions, conditionals and loops, reject invalid input without an unexplained traceback, and add type hints to public functions — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can build a file-reading CLI that validates input and writes a report, run a pytest suite with one command covering happy paths and invalid files, and show a refactoring commit that shrinks a first-version function.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently ship a Python service or pipeline with a committed dependency file, lint/format config, and README commands that reproduce a clean checkout — with tests that assert a named failure mode, not only the happy path.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a failure where a traceback, a missing dependency, or a silent except would mislead, name the packaging or test gap, and produce a README another engineer can follow to install, run tests, and invoke the entry point.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's Python project, name a brittle test or a function that hides I/O behind an untestable shape, and teach when to catch an exception versus let it propagate on an unfamiliar codebase.
